newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche sees full-year profit double H1.
newsitem.headline: Porsche sees full-year profit double H1.

text.p: German sports car maker Porsche AG on Wednesday said it expected profits for the current 1996-97 business year to July 31 to be at least double profits for the first half of the year.
After a day in which Porsche rejected a profits outlook issued by BW Bank, Porsche finance director Holger Haerter said: "We expect in the current year to at least double the half-year result."
In the first half, Porsche posted a group profit after tax of 38.4 million marks, up from 10.3 million marks in the same period a year earlier. Group net profits in 1995-96 were 48.1 million marks.
Porsche had earlier rejected statement from BW Bank which was attributed to Haerter speaking at an investment seminar in the southern German city of Stuttgart.
BW Bank had quoted him saying sales would rise to 3.6 billion marks this year from 2.8 billion marks last year, while net profits would cross the 100 million marks threshold.
